scope: Corollary 9.2 (Lookup approximation of conditional averages) of the manuscript “Buffered comparison and stopping-band resolution in critical Ising” (preprints/Buffered-comparison-and-stopping-band-resolution-in-critical-Ising-September-23-2026/paper.pdf), one of the manuscripts of result family 218 of openai/math at commit 1581d4cbdd69. The statement is quoted verbatim from the text that pdftotext 24.02.0 (-raw -enc UTF-8) extracts from the PDF (SHA-256 d5167e3fe5fb85f4), with whitespace normalised, and was found there under this heading on PDF page 41. Text extraction flattens typeset mathematics (superscripts, subscripts, fractions, large operators, delimiters), so the quote can read differently from the typeset statement and can carry characters with no Unicode meaning; the PDF is authoritative. Finding the quote shows that the manuscript states it, not that it is true. AMVO has checked nothing about this claim.
statement: In the outward setting of The- orem 9.1, let Fδ be the stopping information. For any family of target observables hδ satisfying |hδ| ≤ H, define ai(δ) = EQi,δ hδ (i ≥ 1), and choose any exceptional-bin value in [−H, H]. Then, on every good transcript, E[hδ | Fδ ] − aZδ (δ) ≤ 2Hη. (9.1) In particular, in the reference chart, E E[hδ | Fδ ] − aZδ (δ) 2 ≤ 4H2 (η2 + ϵ). (9.2) The good bins, barriers, and mesh threshold work for all these observables simultaneously. Neither the observables nor their lookup values need converge as δ ↓ 0. More explicitly, fix a reference continuation law ν and regard fν δ (T) = Eν[hδ | Fδ = T] as a function of the stopping transcript T. Evaluating this same function under any buffered band distribution with density bound K gives the integrated estimate with exceptional term Kϵ. It is the reference conditional-average function that is transferred. It also equals the conditional average for the new law when that law has the same continuation and distant wall given T. If the distant wall is changed to an assignment b, the uniform wall extension in Lemma 8.1 supplies the corresponding completed laws Qb i,δ. The conditional averages for this continuation use the separate lookup values ab i (δ) = EQb i,δ hδ.
